<thought>To determine the number of methyl (CH₃) groups in the unknown sample, the most direct approach is to obtain its ¹³C NMR spectrum, which shows distinct carbon environments. Methyl carbons typically appear in the upfield region (≈10–30 ppm). By counting the number of separate signals in this region, we can infer how many unique methyl carbon environments are present, which corresponds to the number of methyl groups in the molecule (assuming no symmetry that makes multiple methyls equivalent). Therefore, I will request the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
